<explanation>
To draw an accurate, detailed system‑design diagram for mGBA, follow these steps:

1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   • mGBA is a cross‑platform emulator tool for Game Boy Advance, Game Boy, and Game Boy Color.  
   • It provides multiple front‑ends (Qt GUI, SDL, CLI), feature modules (recording, scripting, debugging), a core emulation engine, and platform abstraction layers.

2. Analyze the file structure to extract architectural layers  
   • Front‑end layer:  
     – src/platform/qt … (Qt GUI)  
     – src/platform/sdl … (SDL frontend)  
     – src/platform/python … (Python bindings)  
     – src/platform/example, src/platform/headless… (CLI/test executables)  
   • Feature layer:  
     – src/feature/* (command‑line parser, GUI runner, video‑backend, FFmpeg recorder, cheat management, scripting proxy, updater)  
   • Core emulation layer:  
     – src/arm, src/sm83 (CPU decoders/emitters: ARM7TDMI, SM83)  
     – src/gb, src/gba (system cores: memory, I/O, PPU, APU, DMA, timers, BIOS emulation)  
     – src/core (common subsystems: configuration, threading, lockstep, tile/memory caches, sync, rewind, scripting host)  
     – src/debugger (CLI debugger, GDB stub)  
   • Scripting layer:  
     – src/script (embedded Lua engine, scripting API: canvas, input, storage, console)  
   • Platform abstraction layer:  
     – src/platform/posix, windows, 3ds, switch, wii, psp2, libretro, opengl (file I/O/VFS, threading, graphics, audio, input drivers)  
   • Third‑party libraries:  
     – include/mgba‑util, src/third‑party/* (zlib, libpng, SQLite3, FFmpeg, rapidjson, ini parser, LZMA, Discord RPC)  
   • Test/ROM suites:  
     – cinema/… (automated compliance tests)  
     – src/*/test (unit tests for core, GB, GBA, util, debugger)  
   • Build system:  
     – CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, version.cmake

3. Examine the README for technical stack and interactions  
   • Core C/C++ emulator built with CMake.  
   • Optional features toggled by presence of Qt, SDL2, FFmpeg, libpng, zlib, SQLite3, Lua, libelf, json‑c.  
   • Docker, MSYS2, Visual Studio, native toolchain instructions indicate the build and deployment architecture.  
   • Scripting (Lua) hooks into core via src/core/scripting.c and exposes APIs under src/script.

4. Define diagram components and interactions  
   a. Main components (boxes):  
      – Front‑ends: Qt GUI, SDL frontend, Python bindings, CLI/Headless stub  
      – Feature modules: Command‑line parser, GUI runner, FFmpeg recorder, Video backend, Audio backend, Cheat manager, Updater, Scripting proxy  
      – Emulator Core: CPU cores (ARM7TDMI, SM83), System cores (GBA, GB), Memory/Tile caches, Lockstep & Sync, Rewind, Input, I/O, PPU, APU, DMA, Timers, BIOS  
      – Debugger: CLI debugger, GDB remote stub  
      – Scripting Engine: Lua host, script APIs (canvas, storage, input)  
      – Platform Abstraction: VFS, OS threads, OpenGL/SDL2, audio drivers, gamepad input, file dialogs  
      – Third‑party Libraries: zlib, libpng, SQLite3, FFmpeg, RapidJSON, ini‑parser, LZMA SDK, Discord RPC  
      – Test Harness & ROM loader (cinema)  
   b. Relationships (arrows):  
      – Front‑ends → Feature modules (user commands, UI events)  
      – Feature modules → Emulator Core (configuration, run/stop, hooking backends)  
      – Emulator Core → Platform Abstraction (render frame buffer via OpenGL/SDL2, output audio samples, read/write files, lock threads)  
      – Emulator Core ↔ Scripting Engine (script invokes emulator APIs; core calls script callbacks)  
      – Debugger ↔ Emulator Core (inspect/modify memory & registers; GDB stub sends packets over TCP)  
      – Feature modules → Third‑party libraries (FFmpeg recorder uses ffmpeg libs; SQLite3 for game DB; zlib/libpng for savestates; ini parser for configs)  
      – Test Harness uses Emulator Core and Platform Abstraction in headless mode, runs ROMs from cinema/

5. Highlight architectural patterns and design principles  
   • Layered architecture: UI → Feature → Core → Platform.  
   • Plug‑in‑style feature modules: backends for audio/video, scripting, debugging.  
   • Abstraction and separation: CPU decoders, system cores, common core services.  
   • Dependency inversion: Core interfaces define behavior; API clients register as backends.  
   • Cross‑platform via thin platform layer and CMake toolchain files.

6. Tailor diagram to emulator tool specifics  
   • Emphasize multi‑front‑end support.  
   • Show configurable backends for video/audio/recording.  
   • Highlight CPU/subsystem separation (ARM vs. SM83 vs. GBA/GB).  
   • Depict integration with Lua scripting and GDB remote.  
   • Include test runner harness pointing at cinema/ test ROM directories.

7. Diagram styling guidelines  
   • Draw each component as a rectangular box.  
   • Use distinct colors/shapes:  
     – Blue boxes for Front‑end & UI  
     – Green for Feature modules  
     – Red for Core emulation  
     – Orange for Platform Abstraction  
     – Purple for Third‑party libraries  
     – Gray for Test harness  
   • Label each box clearly (e.g., “CPU Core: ARM7TDMI”, “Qt GUI Frontend”).  
   • Draw directional arrows with arrowheads to indicate call or data flow.  
   • Annotate arrows with short descriptions (e.g., “video frames”, “audio samples”, “GDB packets”, “script API calls”).  
   • Optionally group related boxes into swimlanes or layers (UI, Feature, Core, Platform, Libraries, Tests).  
   • Include a legend explaining color coding and arrow types (synchronous vs. asynchronous).

Final checklist before you draw:  
- Capture all layers (UI → Feature → Core → Platform → Libraries).  
- Distinguish CPU cores (ARM7TDMI vs. SM83) and system cores (GBA vs. GB).  
- Show backends (video, audio, recorder) as plug‑ins.  
- Include scripting and debugging as side‑channels into the core.  
- Represent the build system (CMake) as an ancillary box or note if desired.  
- Ensure arrows show the correct direction of control vs. data.  

By following these steps and guidelines, you will produce a detailed, accurate architecture diagram reflecting mGBA’s multi‑layered, plugin‑friendly emulator design.
